verdict.rationale: GitBook ships a first-party built-in GitBook Agent that identifies missing or outdated content, drafts improvements, reviews change requests and auto-translates docs, so delegating documentation tasks to an in-product AI is documented. The evidence is mostly feature titles and marketing lines, with no detail on how users assign arbitrary tasks or how much autonomy the agent has. The reader-facing GitBook Assistant answers questions rather than taking tasks, so it adds little here. Missing for 10: documentation of a general task-delegation interface (prompting or assigning arbitrary edits to the agent), detail on agent autonomy and approval flow, independent or hands-on corroboration that delegation works.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product
